options.text: Matter from one place to another
Energy from one place to another without transferring matter
Mass from one place to another
Particles from one place to another

questions.explanation: Waves transfer energy from one place to another without transferring matter. The particles of the medium oscillate but do not travel with the wave.

questions.stem: What is the amplitude of a wave?

options.text: The distance between two consecutive crests
The maximum displacement from the rest position
The number of waves per second

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a point on a wave from its rest (equilibrium) position. Larger amplitude means the wave carries more energy.

options.text: The number of waves produced per second
The distance between two consecutive points in phase
The time for one complete wave to pass a point

questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive points that are in phase, such as from one crest to the next crest, or one trough to the next trough.
Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz means one complete wave passes a point per second.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between frequency (f) and period (T)?
questions.explanation: Frequency and period are reciprocals of each other: f = 1/T. A wave with a period of 0.5 s has a frequency of 1/0.5 = 2 Hz.

questions.stem: A wave has a frequency of 5 Hz. What is its period?
questions.explanation: T = 1/f = 1/5 = 0.2 s. The period is the time for one complete wave cycle.

questions.stem: If the amplitude of a wave is increased, which property changes?

options.text: The speed of the wave increases
The energy carried by the wave increases

questions.explanation: A greater amplitude means the wave carries more energy. Changing the amplitude does not affect wavelength, frequency, or speed.
